question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode="none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress Gateway binds, and if so what explicit guard or acknowledgement boundary is required?
rationale: Current code intentionally blocks this reachable unauthenticated Gateway shape, and the request would move operator-surface protection from OpenClaw auth to external network controls.

options.title: Keep fail-closed by default
options.body: Maintain the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable binds and only revisit this with a sponsored private-ingress security design.

options.title: Sponsor a dangerous private-ingress opt-in
options.body: Add a named config or CLI acknowledgement for non-loopback no-auth with clear audit findings, docs, and focused startup/runtime tests.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: If maintainers do not want this trust model in core, close the issue and point users to token/password or trusted-proxy deployments.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed by default
recommendation.body: Maintain the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable binds and only revisit this with a sponsored private-ingress security design.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to recent Gateway auth hardening and merger history around the current exposed-startup security boundary.
